text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Police recommend charges against three top officials in government corruption scandal, state attorney's office has reservations.
- Number of foreign workers to be cut to 17,500 within five years, Palestinian quota to rise to 70,000.
- Closure clamped on West Bank after warnings of suicide attacks.
- Finance Minister Meridor proposes the budget be cut despite Bank of Israel Governor Frenkel's refusal to lower interest rates.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Warnings of terrorist attacks in Israel.
- Tension ahead of state attorney's decision on whether to indict in government corruption scandal.
- National unity government on hold.
- Differences between finance minister and central bank governor over rate cut.
- Bank of Israel Governor Frenkel not expected to lower interest rates following high monthly inflation figure.
MAARIV
- Officer in charge of police probe of suspected government corruption says there were attempts to bring political pressure on the investigators.
- Industry and Trade Minister Sharansky opposes cancelling preferential treatment for Israeli products in tenders by state-owned companies.
- U.S. envoy Ross arrives today and will try to push Clinton initiative on reviving Israeli-PLO peace talks.
GLOBES
- Scitex and British Telecom in advanced negotiations on joint communications project for print and graphics industry.
- Cabinet could discuss this week Treasury proposals to cut government expenditures.
JERUSALEM POST
- Police hand in Bar-On findings.
- West Bank under closure.
